attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own Substack post. He characterises LeCun's post rather than quoting it as his claim.

semantics.note: Faithful to the two parts: LeCun is among the hardest pushers against the Act, and his post was a flagrant lie. It is a heavily evaluative observation, but its factual core (whether the chronology in the post was false) is checkable.

contract.note: The plain readings are ordinary: 'among the most prominent opponents' and 'obvious material falsehood', with a weaker no-intent reading allowed. The December 1–12 window is the evaluator's choice. The result still depends on what 'added late' referred to, and the evidence does not recover that.

evidence.note: Official Council draft dated May 13, 2022 with general-purpose AI provisions. It shows an earlier antecedent, but without LeCun's full post it cannot show his chronology was false. It also predates the target period.
TIME, Nov 22, 2023: names other opponents (Aleph Alpha, Mistral, France/Germany). It does not rank LeCun, and it predates the target period.

reviews.rationale: LeCun's complete post was not recovered, so we cannot tell what 'added late' referred to or whether it was false. There is no comparative record of advocacy for December 1–12, 2023, and no evidence of knowing deception. The 2022 draft and the TIME report are context only. The evidence does not settle either part of the claim.
